author: mikeyzhang75
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

body:
## 📱 모바일 최적화 및 UX 개선

  이번 PR에서는 사용자 경험을 대폭 개선하고 모바일 환경에서의 사용성을 향상시켰습니다.

  ### 🎯 주요 개선 사항

  #### 1. 냉장고 관리 모달화
  - **기존**: 별도 페이지로 이동하여 재료 관리
  - **개선**: 레시피 페이지에서 바로 모달로 냉장고 관리 가능
  - 페이지 이동 없이 빠른 재료 추가/삭제

  #### 2. 스마트 재료 검색 및 추가 시스템
  - **기존 재료 우선**: 데이터베이스의 기존 재료 목록에서 검색
  - **클릭 추가**: 검색 결과를 클릭만으로 간편 추가
  - **커스텀 재료**: 검색 결과가 없으면 새 재료 생성 가능
  - **직접 입력**: 빠른 입력을 위한 텍스트 입력 방식도 유지

  #### 3. 컴포넌트 아키텍처 개선
  - **페이지별 컴포넌트**: `/components/recipes/`, `/components/fridge/`
  - **공통 컴포넌트**: `/components/common/`
  - **재사용성 향상**: LoadingSpinner, EmptyState, Modal 등
  - **유지보수성 개선**: 관심사 분리 및 단일 책임 원칙

  #### 4. 모바일 UI/UX 최적화
  - **텍스트 대비 개선**: 모든 텍스트가 배경과 충분한 대비
  - **터치 친화적**: 모바일에서 호버 대신 클릭/탭 기반 인터랙션
  - **드롭다운 개선**: 모바일에서 정확한 위치에 표시되는 커스텀 드롭다운
  - **레시피 카드**: 더 큰 썸네일과 확장 가능한 재료 목록

  #### 5. 기능 버그 수정
  - **재료 삭제**: undefined ID 문제 해결
  - **새 재료 추가**: 검색 모달에서 커스텀 재료 추가 기능 수정
  - **API 엔드포인트**: 누락된 DELETE 엔드포인트 구현

  ### 🛠 기술적 개선사항

  - **Repository 패턴**: API 로직을 별도 Repository로 분리
  - **TypeScript 타입 안정성**: 모든 컴포넌트에 적절한 타입 정의
  - **ESLint 규칙**: 코딩 스타일 통일 및 품질 향상
  - **모바일 퍼스트**: 반응형 디자인으로 모든 화면 크기 지원

  ### 📊 사용자 경험 개선

  - **재료 관리 시간**: 평균 3-4회 클릭으로 단축
  - **검색 효율성**: 기존 재료 우선 추천으로 일관성 증대
  - **모바일 사용성**: 터치 기반 인터랙션으로 직관성 향상
  - **시각적 피드백**: 명확한 버튼 상태 및 로딩 표시

  ### 📝 Test plan
  - [ ] 레시피 페이지에서 냉장고 모달 열기/닫기 테스트
  - [ ] 재료 검색 및 추가 기능 테스트
  - [ ] 기존 재료 삭제 기능 테스트
  - [ ] 모바일 환경에서 드롭다운 위치 확인
  - [ ] 텍스트 가독성 확인 (특히 input 필드)
  - [ ] 레시피 카드 확장/축소 기능 테스트

author: musdom
body:
Enables Secure Boot v2 on Frostsnaps without disabling boot mode. Production Frontiers will be locked down. Backwards compatible with dev Alpha devices.

In addition to checks listed in https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/v5.1.6/esp32c3/security/secure-boot-v2.html#verify-signature-block, the app firmware updater will verify new firmware before switching the active partition.

To test SB in this PR
1. Install esptool https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esptool/en/latest/esp32/installation.html so you can use espsecure.py
2. Get secure_boot_signing_key.pem from me. Otherwise you have to build and sign your own bootloader.
3. `just flash-secure-new` if enabling SB on new devices, which will flash bootloader.bin and partitions.bin
4. `just flash-secure` to sign and flash new firmware
5. `just monitor` and Ctrl+R to see expected secure boot status in the bootloader logs:

```
I (281) esp_image: Verifying image signature...
I (282) secure_boot_v2: Verifying with RSA-PSS...
I (285) secure_boot_v2: Signature verified successfully!
I (287) boot: Loaded app from partition at offset 0x160000
I (293) secure_boot_v2: enabling secure boot v2...
I (298) secure_boot_v2: secure boot v2 is already enabled, continuing..
```

Dev devices must `just flash` to be on the new partition table and bootloader-dev.bin.
 
Todo: 
1. Rewrite espsecure.py in Rust for frostsnap-factory
2. Make a test firmware signature block with correct RSA public key hash but wrong signature.
3. Make a production bootloader for Frontier devices

body:
## Summary
- Replaces complex retainable card logic with elegant functional composition approach
- Cards create rent adjustment functions using `:card.rent/multiplier` and `:card.rent/dice-multiplier` 
- Move function accepts optional `:rent-adjustment` parameter (defaults to `identity`)
- Applied cleanly with `(rent-adjustment rent)` during rent payment
- Zero changes needed to existing rent calculation logic in `util.clj`

## Key Changes
- **Card definitions**: Updated utility/railroad cards to use new `:card.rent/*` format
- **Cards namespace**: Rent adjustment function creation using `cond` pattern
- **Core namespace**: Enhanced `move-to-cell` to accept `:rent-adjustment` parameter
- **Transaction tracking**: Added `:rent/original` and `:rent/adjustment` fields for audit trail
- **Comprehensive testing**: 10 new tests covering function creation, integration, edge cases, regression, and transaction history

## Test Coverage
- Function creation and behavior validation
- Integration with card system and game state
- Edge case handling (unowned properties, errors)
- Regression testing (normal cards still work)
- Transaction history verification (audit trail)

All 48 tests pass with 1438 assertions.

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: rmoh777
body:
## Problem Solved

The current AI processing was artificially limited to 8,000 characters, which meant only ~15% of typical filing content was being analyzed. For complex filings like the recent Breezeline case (53K characters), this resulted in incomplete AI summaries despite successful document extraction.

## Key Enhancement

**Character Limit Increase**: 8,000  60,000 characters (7.5x improvement)

### Before vs After Impact
- **Typical filing** (20-40K chars): 20-50% analyzed  100% analyzed
- **Complex filings** (50K+ chars): 15% analyzed  100% analyzed  
- **Breezeline example**: 53K chars  previously 8K analyzed, now 53K analyzed

## Technical Implementation

**File Modified**: cron-worker/src/lib/ai/gemini-enhanced.js

**Change**: Replace hardcoded 8K limit with intelligent 60K limit:
`javascript
// OLD: Arbitrary 8K truncation


// NEW: Comprehensive 60K analysis with safety limit
const maxChars = 60000;
const truncatedText = documentText.length > maxChars 
    ? documentText.substring(0, maxChars) + '\\n\\n... [Content truncated for length]'
    : documentText;
`

## Performance & Cost Analysis

### Processing Impact
- **Time increase**: ~2-3 seconds per filing
- **Overall BAU runtime**: 70s  ~80s (well within limits)
- **Memory/Network**: Negligible impact

### Cost Impact  
- **Current**: ~.25/month for AI processing
- **Enhanced**: ~.80/month for AI processing
- **Increase**: ~.55/month for dramatically better analysis

### ROI Justification
- **Cost**: ~/month increase
- **Benefit**: Complete document analysis vs 15% truncated summaries
- **User value**: Comprehensive regulatory intelligence instead of incomplete analysis
- **Competitive advantage**: Full-document AI analysis vs basic keyword extraction

## Expected Outcomes

### Immediate Benefits
1. **Complete Analysis**: Users get insights from entire document content
2. **Better Key Points**: AI can identify important details from all sections
3. **Improved Confidence**: AI analysis based on full context, not fragments
4. **Enhanced Value Prop**: Delivers on promise of comprehensive regulatory intelligence

### Quality Improvements
- **Multi-document filings**: All documents fully analyzed instead of first document only
- **Complex agreements**: Full contractual terms analyzed, not just headers
- **Technical specifications**: Complete technical details included in analysis
- **Regulatory context**: Full background and implications captured

## Safety Measures

- **60K limit**: Prevents extreme cases while leveraging Gemini 1.5 Flash's 1M token capacity
- **Graceful truncation**: Clear messaging when rare 60K+ content is encountered
- **Backward compatibility**: No breaking changes to existing functionality

## Testing Validation

-  **Syntax validated**: Clean compilation
-  **Logic verified**: Proper truncation handling
-  **Safety confirmed**: Reasonable limits maintained

This enhancement directly addresses user feedback about incomplete AI summaries and positions SimpleDCC as providing truly comprehensive regulatory intelligence analysis.

body:
Many developers will be surprised to learn that `requests` library calls do not include timeouts by default. This means that an attempted request could hang indefinitely if no connection is established or if no data is received from the server. 

The [requests documentation](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user/advanced/#timeouts) suggests that most calls should explicitly include a `timeout` parameter. This codemod adds a default timeout value in order to set an upper bound on connection times and ensure that requests connect or fail in a timely manner. This value also ensures the connection will timeout if the server does not respond with data within a reasonable amount of time. 

While timeout values will be application dependent, we believe that this codemod adds a reasonable default that serves as an appropriate ceiling for most situations. 

Our changes look like the following:
```diff
 import requests
 
- requests.get("http://example.com")
+ requests.get("http://example.com", timeout=60)
```

author: nikhilkumawat03
body:
### Issue Description:

Fuzz testing revealed a RuntimeException in LeveledManifest.maxBytesForLevel during repair operations when compaction parameters cause the calculated maximum bytes for a level to exceed Long.MAX_VALUE (9,223,372,036,854,775,807). The error occurs with inputs like fanout_size=90, sstable_size_in_mb=1088, and level=8, resulting in Math.pow(90, 8) * 1141899264 ≈ 4.9155 × 10²⁴, which exceeds Long.MAX_VALUE. The issue arises because LeveledCompactionStrategy does not validate these parameters during table creation, allowing invalid configurations to persist until repair.

### The original error (from LeveledManifest.java):
`java.lang.RuntimeException: At most 9223372036854775807 bytes may be in a compaction level; your maxSSTableSize must be absurdly high to compute 4.915501902751334E24`

This PR adds proactive validation in LeveledCompactionStrategy.validateOptions to ensure fanout_size and sstable_size_in_mb do not cause an overflow, throwing a ConfigurationException during CREATE TABLE or ALTER TABLE instead of failing later during repair.
 
### Example which created issue during fuzz testing ([CASSANDRA-20570](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/CASSANDRA-20570))

```
CREATE KEYSPACE test WITH replication = {'class': 'SimpleStrategy', 'replication_factor': 1};
CREATE TABLE test.table1 (k int PRIMARY KEY, v int)
    WITH compaction = {
        'class': 'LeveledCompactionStrategy',
        'fanout_size': '90',
        'sstable_size_in_mb': '1088'
    };
```
Patch by: Nikhil Kumawat;
Reviewed by: TBD
JIRA: [CASSANDRA-20570](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/CASSANDRA-20570)

body:
This PR removes the `Update` method from the `InputModelProperty` class and all its associated tests.

## Background

The `Update` method was added to allow modification of input model properties after creation, but as noted in the issue, input types should barely need to be updated. The method provided unnecessary mutability that goes against the intended design.

## Changes Made

1. **Removed `InputModelProperty.Update` method** - The entire method (lines 23-97) including its comprehensive documentation and parameter validation logic has been removed from `/packages/http-client-csharp/generator/Microsoft.TypeSpec.Generator.Input/src/InputTypes/InputModelProperty.cs`

2. **Removed all related tests** - All 12 test methods that tested the `Update` functionality have been removed from `InputModelPropertyTests.cs`, reducing the test count from 24 to 12 tests

3. **No production code impact** - Analysis confirmed that the `Update` method was only used in test code, not in any production scenarios

## Verification

- All core generator tests (1005 tests) continue to pass
- Build succeeds without any compilation errors
- No breaking changes to the public API surface beyond the intended removal

This change simplifies the API and aligns with the principle that input types should be immutable after creation.

Fixes #7941.

author: jbmiller10
body:
## Summary

This PR implements the multi-collection search API as part of the Semantik v2.0 collections refactor. The new search endpoints enable searching across multiple collections with result aggregation and re-ranking.

## Implementation Details

### New Endpoints
- `POST /api/v2/search` - Multi-collection search supporting up to 10 collections
- `POST /api/v2/search/single` - Single collection search (backward compatibility)

### Key Features
- **Parallel Search**: Collections are searched in parallel using `asyncio.gather()`
- **Automatic Re-ranking**: When collections use different embedding models, results are automatically re-ranked
- **Partial Failure Handling**: If some collections fail, results from successful collections are still returned
- **Comprehensive Metrics**: Timing information for search, re-ranking, and total operation time
- **Rate Limiting**: 30 req/min for multi-collection, 60 req/min for single collection

### Technical Implementation
- Created new v2 schemas with collection-aware result metadata
- Implemented federated search with result merging
- Added collection access validation using `CollectionRepository`
- Integrated with existing re-ranking infrastructure
- Full error handling with graceful degradation

## Test Plan

- [x] Unit tests for collection access validation
- [x] Tests for single collection search with retry logic
- [x] Tests for result re-ranking functionality
- [x] Tests for multi-collection search with partial failures
- [x] Tests for backward compatibility endpoints
- [x] All code quality checks passing (black, ruff, mypy)
- [x] 10 out of 11 tests passing

## Dependencies

This task depends on TASK-015 (Collection API Routes) which has been completed.

## Part of Collections Refactor Phase 4

This is a critical component of the v2.0 architecture, enabling the core value proposition of searching across multiple distinct collections.

body:
## 📋 概要

暗号化・難読化対応のセーブデータインポート・エクスポート機能を実装しました。
ユーザーがゲームデータを安全にバックアップ・共有できるようになります。

## 🎯 主要機能

### 暗号化システム
- **XOR暗号化 + BASE64エンコード**による難読化
- **ゲーム固有キー**を使用した暗号化（レベル・転生回数・ランダムシードから生成）
- **チェックサム検証**による整合性チェック
- **バージョン管理**（SGKT_v1フォーマット）

### エクスポート機能
- ワンクリックでセーブデータをテキストファイルとしてダウンロード
- ファイル名: `sugoroku-save-YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS.txt`
- 暗号化済みデータの自動生成

### インポート機能
- ファイル選択またはドラッグ&ドロップでのインポート
- インポート前の自動バックアップ作成
- データ検証・復号化処理
- 確認ダイアログによる安全性確保

### UI統合
- 統計モーダルの設定タブに「データ管理」セクション追加
- アニメーション付きフィードバック
- レスポンシブ対応
- 既存デザインとの統一性

## 🔧 技術仕様

### ファイル構成
- `src/utils/crypto-utils.ts` - 暗号化・復号化ユーティリティ
- `src/data/storage-manager.ts` - インポート・エクスポート機能追加
- `src/ui/ui-manager.ts` - UI処理・イベントハンドラー追加
- `index.html` - データ管理UI追加
- `assets/css/style.css` - スタイル追加

### セキュリティ仕様
- **フォーマット**: `SGKT_v1_[BASE64暗号化データ]`
- **キー生成**: `SUGOROKU_${hash(level_rebirthCount_boardRandomSeed)}`
- **整合性**: SHA-256風の簡易チェックサム
- **難読化**: 一般ユーザーには読解困難なレベル

## 🎨 UI/UX改善

### 新規UI要素
- 📤 データエクスポートボタン

author: dkropachev
body:
Fix: https://github.com/scylladb/python-driver/issues/503

This issue happens when connection is opened and closed right away.
`_loop_will_run` calls `conn.close` on it, which removes `self._read_watcher` from the `connection` and since connection stays in `self._new_conns` on next iteration it will pick it up and try to start `self._read_watcher` on it.
Solution is to remove closed connection from `self._new_conns` and check if `self._read_watcher` is not None before starting it.

Two fixes for follwing problem:
```
Exception ignored in: <bound method LibevLoop._loop_will_run of <cassandra.io.libevreactor.LibevLoop object at 0x7343276afc10>>
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/123/cassandra/io/libevreactor.py", line 197, in _loop_will_run
    conn._read_watcher.start()
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'start'
```
1. Check if `self._read_watcher` is not `None` before starting it
2. Remove connection from `self._new_conns` when it is destroyed

body:
On some systems, the .profile file already sources .bashrc so telling the user to source .profile in their .bashrc creates a loop. Furthermore, given that on some systems the .bashrc is already sourced in the .profile, it makes it more like for users to copy the opam incantation in their .bashrc but forget to remove it from the .profile, leading to a doubling of some environment variables and a loss of track of some of them by `opam env` (aka. https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6455)

Fixes https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/5819
Fixes https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/4201
Fixes https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/3990

## #️⃣ Issue Number

<!-- 관련된 이슈 번호를 작성해주세요. 예: #12, #34 없다면 무시 -->

---

## 📝 요약(Summary)

meeting/{eventId}/coordinate/my -> 나의 가능한 시간대 분리
meeting/{eventId}/coordinate -> 함께 가능한 시간
유저 정보 스토어 저장 -> 스토리지 활용
타임비트 연산 함수 추가
토스트 컴포넌트 생성 -> 오류시 출력될 토스트
추가)
일정 등록 시 30분 단위인거 1시간 단위로 수정조치

- [x] 코드 리팩토링
- [ ] 주석 추가 및 수정
- [ ] 문서 수정
- [ ] 테스트 추가, 테스트 리팩토링
- [ ] 빌드 부분 혹은 패키지 매니저 수정
- [ ] 파일 혹은 폴더명 수정
- [ ] 파일 혹은 폴더 삭제

---

## 📸스크린샷 (선택)
![chrome-capture-2025-07-17](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/89d5630c-dcb1-4e48-8b62-0c2b25141b1f)

---

## 💬 공유사항 to 리뷰어

함께 가능한 시간대, 나의 시간대 확정 부분의 API 가 과도하게 사용될것 같아서 페이지 분리.

meeting/{eventId}/coordinate/my -> 나의 가능한 시간대
meeting/{eventId}/coordinate -> 함께 가능한 시간

나의 시간대, 함꼐 시간대 컴포넌트 별도로 분리 작업
해당 컴포넌트에 과도한 기능작업이 되어있어 재활용하기엔 무리가 있다고 판단

나의 시간대 작업 등에서 유저 정보가 필요하여 member/me 를 호출한 이후로 store 에 저장
app/stores/useAuthStores
-> "use client" 를 사용한 페이지에서 사용가능
-> 서버 컴포넌트로 작성된곳에선 사용 불가

타임비트 연산 함수 추가
utils/timebitFormat.ts
`convertHexBitToTimes()` 은 `"000003FC0000"` 이 값을 `["09:00", "09:30", ...]` 형식으로 변환
`convertTimesToHexBit()` 은 `["09:00", "09:30", ...]` 이 값을 `000003FC0000` 형식으로 변환

토스트 컴포넌트 생성 
오류 상황에서 출력할 토스트 정보를 담고 있음
message 를 매개변수로 받음
src/components/ui/Toast.ts


추후 시간표는 리팩토링예정
# ~~30분 단위로 지정된 일정은 테스트 해봐야 함~~
~~제대로 안나오므로 수정 진행중~~

# 30분 단위로 일정 등록 과정 수정
30분 단위로 등록시 시간표의 디자인 자체가 깨지고 계산이 더 복잡해지므로 1시간 단위로 수정 조치
일정 등록은 1시간 단위 이고 가능한 시간 선택은 30분 단위로 선택 가능

body:
## Summary

- **DisplayFlex Layout System**: Created reusable DisplayFlex and DisplayFlexItem components with comprehensive props for flexible layouts
- **Enhanced AI Assistant UX**: Updated button icon to Sparkles (✨) and improved placeholder text to encourage discovery
- **Radix UI Migration**: Migrated Toolbar link dialog to use Radix UI Dialog primitives for better accessibility
- **Layout Improvements**: Fixed RichTextEditor footer spacing using DisplayFlex components with proper justify and gap controls

## Key Features Added

### 🎨 DisplayFlex Layout Components
- Comprehensive props: `gap`, `align`, `justify`, `direction`, `wrap`
- Type-safe with predefined spacing scales (`xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`)
- DisplayFlexItem with individual flex controls (`grow`, `shrink`, `basis`, `align`)
- Clean CSS modules implementation with modifier classes

### ✨ AI Assistant Enhancements  
- Changed icon from `Bot` to `Sparkles` for more magical/AI feel
- Updated placeholder text to "✨ Try the AI Assistant button for inspiration\!"
- Improved discoverability and user engagement
- Better visual hierarchy in footer layout

### 🔧 Technical Improvements

body:
Many developers will be surprised to learn that `requests` library calls do not include timeouts by default. This means that an attempted request could hang indefinitely if no connection is established or if no data is received from the server. 

The [requests documentation](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user/advanced/#timeouts) suggests that most calls should explicitly include a `timeout` parameter. This codemod adds a default timeout value in order to set an upper bound on connection times and ensure that requests connect or fail in a timely manner. This value also ensures the connection will timeout if the server does not respond with data within a reasonable amount of time. 

While timeout values will be application dependent, we believe that this codemod adds a reasonable default that serves as an appropriate ceiling for most situations. 

Our changes look like the following:
```diff
 import requests
 
- requests.get("http://example.com")
+ requests.get("http://example.com", timeout=60)
```

author: yjsoon
body:
## Summary
- Introduces web worker support for CPU-intensive tasks: PDF generation and CSV/TSV parsing
- Adds React hooks `usePdfWorker` and `useCsvWorker` for easy integration
- Provides a demo component `WebWorkerExample` showcasing usage and progress UI
- Includes detailed documentation on implementation, architecture, and integration

## Changes

### Web Worker Implementation
- **PDF Generator Worker** (`public/workers/pdf-generator.worker.js`): Offloads PDF creation to a worker thread with font caching, progress updates, and support for custom fonts
- **CSV Parser Worker** (`public/workers/csv-parser.worker.js`): Parses CSV/TSV files asynchronously with format detection, header and email column detection, and progress reporting

### React Hooks
- **usePdfWorker**: Manages PDF worker lifecycle, sends generation requests, handles progress and results
- **useCsvWorker**: Manages CSV worker lifecycle, sends parse requests, handles progress and results

### UI Component
- **WebWorkerExample**: Demonstrates file upload for CSV parsing and button-triggered PDF generation with real-time progress bars and result logs

### Documentation
- Added `docs/WEB_WORKERS_IMPLEMENTATION.md` detailing:
  - Architecture and file structure
  - Worker communication flow
  - Usage examples for hooks
  - Performance benefits and browser compatibility
  - Integration guide for existing code
  - Future enhancement ideas

## Test plan
- [x] Upload CSV files and verify parsing results and progress updates
- [x] Generate sample PDFs and verify file download and progress feedback
- [x] Confirm UI remains responsive during heavy operations
- [x] Review documentation for clarity and completeness

This PR significantly improves app performance and user experience by leveraging multi-threading for heavy tasks.

**Problem**

- Users get an error when trying to use learning mode for a video longer than around 4 hours

**Solution**
- Used a tokenizer library to encode each transcript entry one by one and add it to a new slice only if the token limit hasn't been exceeded yet. This cuts off entries cleanly and makes sure we're not cutting off the middle of a time stamp or something.

- Saves the truncated transcript into redis

author: airdrummingfool
body: ## Proposed change This change adds "state" as an option when selecting secondary entity info to display in the `entities` card. While it might seem redundant, some entity rows show controls as the primary entity info, and in that case there is no way to directly view the entity state. The most common example I can think of (and the specific problem I ran into) is a garage door opener (cover): It is not visually easy to parse whether the door is up or down (granted, if I look a bit closer at the icon or the state of the buttons I can figure it out). With the state displayed in the secondary info area, it is very easy to see: I also find it useful for locks, and for number inputs in the new Sections layout (if the section is narrow, the state is not displayed). ## Type of change - [ ] Dependency upgrade - [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] New feature (thank you!) - [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break) - [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests ## Example configuration Frontend YAML configuration example: ```yaml title: Garage type: entities entities: - entity: cover.garage_door secondary_info: state ``` ## Additional information I found a request for this in the HA forums: https://community.home-assistant.io/t/secondary-info-on-a-cover-entity-row/690657 I'm open to narrowing the scope of the `state` option to just certain domains, but I think it's nice to have as an option for everything. I'm not 100% sure about the parameters to `computeStateDisplay` (mostly the numeric device classes parameter), so please let me know if something doesn't look right. ## Checklist - [x] The code change is tested and works locally. - [x] There is no commented out code in this PR. - [ ] Tests have been added to verify that the new code works. This TEST_TIMEOUT parameter is already used for PC-based tests (eg unix and webassembly ports), and it makes sense for it to be used for bare-metal ports as well.  That way the timeout is configurable for all targets.

body: ### Summary Adds support for connecting to remote Playwright browser instances running in Docker containers for better scalability and isolation. ### Key Changes - Added `PlaywrightConfig` dataclass with url parameter for WebSocket endpoints - Enhanced `get_flights()` and related functions to accept optional `playwright_config` parameter - Modified Playwright modules to connect to remote instances via `playwright.chromium.connect()` - Updated README with Docker setup instructions and usage examples ### Usage ``` from fast_flights import get_flights, PlaywrightConfig playwright_config = PlaywrightConfig(url="ws://localhost:3000") result = get_flights(..., playwright_config=playwright_config) ``` ### Docker Setup ``` docker run -p 3000:3000 mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.53.0-noble \ /bin/bash -c "npx playwright install && npx playwright run-server --port=3000" ``` ### Benefits - now you can run playwright within a docker compose stack for completely headless operation - Container isolation: Browsers run in Docker instead of locally - Deployment flexibility: Can run browsers on different machines - Backward compatible - existing code continues to work unchanged. #### 🤖 LLM Analysis Summary
> #### 🐞 Vulnerability Description
> 이 코드에서는 민감한 정보를 포함할 수 있는 요청을 암호화되지 않은 HTTP 프로토콜을 통해 전송하고 있습니다. 이는 네트워크 상에서 데이터가 중간에 가로채일 위험을 증가시킵니다.
> #### ⚠️ Potential Risks
> 민감한 정보가 네트워크에서 가로채일 수 있으며, 이는 데이터 유출 및 보안 침해로 이어질 수 있습니다.
> #### 🛠 Recommended Fix
> HTTP 대신 HTTPS 프로토콜을 사용하여 데이터를 암호화된 상태로 전송해야 합니다. 이를 통해 데이터 전송 중에 정보가 가로채이는 것을 방지할 수 있습니다.

### **User description** ### What's new #### Content Status Table Normalization Added **github_repository_content_status** table to enable multiple content sources per GitHub repository: - **Why**: A single GitHub repository can now have multiple ingestion sources (Blob/code, Pull Requests, and potentially Issues, Discussions, etc. in the future) - **Normalization**: Instead of tracking a single status per repository, we now track status per content type - **Benefits**: - Each content type can be ingested independently with its own sync state - Different content types can have different update frequencies and retry strategies - Enables gradual rollout of new content types without affecting existing ingestions #### Pull Request Embeddings Added **github_repository_pull_request_embeddings** table: - Stores vector embeddings for PR title/body, comments, and diffs - Uses a `document_key` column (e.g., `123:title_body`, `123:comment:123abcxyz`) to fit the current RAG ingest interface - 📝 Extending the ingest interface to handle composite keys is possible, but the dev & migration cost is high relative to the narrow benefit, so generating a single key is the pragmatic choice ### Implementation Note Indexes are kept minimal in this PR. Additional indexes (e.g., on status columns) will be added as needed when implementing query patterns. ### Deprecations Marks `status`, `errorCode`, `retryAfter`, and `lastIngestedCommitSha` in **github_repository_index** as `@deprecated`. author: copilot
body:
This PR implements a comprehensive chi-square analysis system to identify associations between predictor variables and developmental domain scores in the `datos_optimizados.csv` dataset, addressing the need to understand key risk factors for neurodevelopmental disorders.

## 🎯 Analysis Overview

- **Dataset**: 1,725 observations with 57 variables analyzed
- **Developmental Domains**: 5 domains categorized into risk levels based on Z-scores
- **Statistical Tests**: 29 chi-square tests performed with Bonferroni correction
- **Significant Associations**: 9 associations identified (p < 0.05 after correction)

## 🔬 Key Features Implemented

### Data Processing & Categorization
- **Risk Categories**: Z-scores categorized into three levels:
  - Z ≥ -1: Adequate development
  - -2 ≤ Z < -1: Risk of neurodevelopmental disorders
  - Z < -2: High risk of neurodevelopmental disorders

### Statistical Analysis
- **Chi-square tests** for all predictor-domain combinations
- **Bonferroni correction** for multiple testing
- **Effect sizes** calculated using Cramér's V
- **Robust handling** of sparse contingency tables and missing data

### Visualization & Reporting
- **Heatmaps** showing p-values and effect sizes across all associations
- **Bar charts** for top significant associations
- **Comprehensive reports** with clinical recommendations
- **Export capabilities** for further analysis

## 📊 Key Findings

### Motor Development Most Affected
- **Gross Motor Development**: 6 significant associations
- **Fine Motor Development**: 3 significant associations
- **Other domains**: No significant associations found

### Primary Risk Factors
1. **Nutrition**: Vitamin A and mineral supplementation (strongest associations)
2. **Geographic**: Rural residence (effect size: 0.1092 - strongest single factor)
3. **Age-specific**: Different supplementation effects across age groups

### Top Associations
```
1. Vitamin A (6-12 months) → Gross Motor (χ² = 81.157, p = 2.872e-15)
2. Minerals (6-12 months) → Gross Motor (χ² = 80.873, p = 3.299e-15)
3. Area of Residence → Gross Motor (χ² = 22.558, p = 3.664e-04)
```

## 📁 Files Added

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `chi_square_analysis.py` | Complete analysis implementation |
| `summary_findings.py` | Key findings display script |
| `chi_square_analysis_report.txt` | Detailed written report |
| `chi_square_significant_results.csv` | Significant associations data |
| `chi_square_all_results.csv` | Complete test results |
| `contingency_tables.txt` | Detailed contingency tables |
| `*.png` | Visualization outputs |
| `README.md` | Comprehensive documentation |
| `.gitignore` | Python project maintenance |

## 💡 Clinical Impact

The analysis provides evidence-based recommendations for:
- **Early screening**: Focus on motor development assessment
- **Nutrition interventions**: Ensure adequate vitamin A and mineral supplementation
- **Geographic targeting**: Specialized programs for rural populations
- **Risk stratification**: Multi-factor screening protocols

## 🔧 Technical Implementation

### Robust Statistical Methods
- Expected frequency validation (≥ 5 for valid tests)
- Zero-frequency cell handling
- Comprehensive missing data management
- Multiple testing correction applied

### Code Quality
- Object-oriented design with clear separation of concerns
- Comprehensive error handling
- Extensive documentation and comments
- Modular structure for easy extension

## 🚀 Usage

```python
# Run complete analysis
python chi_square_analysis.py

# View summary findings
python summary_findings.py
```

This implementation provides a solid foundation for understanding neurodevelopmental risk factors and can guide targeted intervention strategies in clinical and public health settings.

*This pull request was created as a result of the following prompt from Copilot chat.*
> Perform comprehensive chi-square analysis on the datos_optimizados.csv dataset to identify associations between all predictor variables and developmental domain scores. 
> 
> The analysis should include:
> 
> 1. **Data Processing:**
>    - Load datos_optimizados.csv
>    - Categorize developmental scores into risk categories:
>      - Z ≥ -1: Adequate development
>      - -2 ≤ Z < -1: Risk of neurodevelopmental disorders
>      - Z < -2: High risk of neurodevelopmental disorders
> 
> 2. **Variables to analyze:**
>    - **Demographics:** edad_meses_nino, edad_anos_madre, edad_anos_padre, grupo_etnico, area_residencia
>    - **Education:** nivel_educativo_madre, nivel_educativo_padre
>    - **Housing conditions:** fuente_agua_consumo, tipo_sanitario, manejo_basura, tipo_energia_luz, tipo_energia_cocina, propiedad_vivienda
>    - **Household characteristics:** sexo_jefe_hogar, situacion_laboral_madre, situacion_laboral_padre, tipo_empleo_madre, tipo_empleo_padre, seguro_social, total_personas_hogar, total_hermanos, posicion_nino_hermanos, estado_civil_cuidador
>    - **Child activities:** horas_pantalla, horas_juego_cuidador
>    - **Prenatal care:** numero_controles_prenatales, ultrasonido_embarazo, prenatales_primeros_3_meses, prenatales_resto_embarazo
>    - **Birth/early care:** servicio_asistencia_parto, tipo_parto, razon_cesarea_emergencia, lactancia_primeros_6_meses, lactancia_6-12_meses, lactancia_12-24_meses
>    - **Nutrition:** vitamina_a_6-12_meses, vitamina_a_12-18_meses, vitamina_a_18-24_meses, vitaminas_minerales_6-12_meses, vitaminas_minerales_12-18_meses, vitaminas_minerales_18-24_meses
>    - **Health outcomes:** retardo_crecimiento, desnutricion_aguda, hospitalizado_neonatal, razon_hospitalizado_neonatal, hospitalizado_infancia, razon_hospitalizado_infancia, vacunacion_completa
> 
> 3. **Developmental domains:**
>    - zscore_desarrollo_comunicacion
>    - zscore_desarrollo_motricidad_gruesa
>    - zscore_desarrollo_motricidad_fina
>    - zscore_desarrollo_resolucion_problemas
>    - zscore_desarrollo_socio_individual
> 
> 4. **Analysis requirements:**
>    - Perform chi-square tests for each variable against each developmental domain
>    - Create contingency tables for significant associations
>    - Generate visualizations (bar plots, heatmaps) for significant results
>    - Calculate effect sizes (Cramér's V) for significant associations

body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack) (oldest at bottom):
* #585
* __->__ #565

We currently have a lot of code duplication for blocking/nonblocking variants.

This PR lets the blocking variants be defined in terms of the async ones.

It first directly exposes the tokio Future object to python, letting it choose to synchronously block on it, or turn it into a asyncio.Future. Then when we are running async code to do pipe receives in a sync context, we can skip running a real event loop and just step the coroutine manually.

TODO: expand writeup.


Currently there is jank around the fact that we are running synchronous actor code on a thread that already has a running event loop. I put in a workaround with a comment, but we should resolve this by not running the sync code on the asyncio loop.

## Contributing Guidelines

We have prepared a `pre-commit` hook to enforce consistent code formatting across the project. If your code complies with the standards, you should not see any errors, you can clean up your code following the steps below:

1. Install the required dependencies:

```shell
    pip install ruff pre-commit
```

2. Then, run the following command before commit:

```shell
    pre-commit run --all-files
```

3. Finally, please double-check your code to ensure it complies with the following additional specifications as much as possible:
  - Avoid hard-coding local paths: Make sure your submissions do not include hard-coded local paths, as these paths are specific to individual development environments and can cause compatibility issues. Use relative paths or configuration files instead.
  - Clear error handling: Implement clear error-handling mechanisms in your code so that error messages can accurately indicate the location of the problem, possible causes, and suggested solutions, facilitating quick debugging.
  - Detailed comments and documentation: Add comments to complex code sections and provide comprehensive documentation to explain the functionality of the code, input-output requirements, and potential error scenarios.

Thank you for your contributions!

author: kevinmehall
body:
For usbccgp devices, nusb collected InterfaceInfo data from the properties of child device nodes, while for other devices it read and parsed the cached configuration descriptor. This changes to doing the latter for all devices, but still iterates usbccgp child nodes to populate cached interface strings when available.

This fixes InterfaceInfo missing interfaces below IADs (which do not have their own device nodes), and means that we should at least have class/subclass/protocol in hotplug events where Windows hasn't created the child device nodes yet (https://github.com/kevinmehall/nusb/issues/149).

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>jackdewinter/pymarkdown (jackdewinter/pymarkdown)</summary>

### [`v0.9.36`](https://redirect.github.com/jackdewinter/pymarkdown/releases/tag/v0.9.36): Version 0.9.36 - 2026-03-15

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jackdewinter/pymarkdown/compare/v0.9.35...v0.9.36)

In this release, we’ve invested heavily in revamping our documentation so that you can get from installation to your first useful scan more quickly. After the last release, a backlog review made it clear that our documentation needed an overhaul, especially for people seeing PyMarkdown for the first time. Over time, we added new sections and details without a full restructuring, which made it harder for new users to see where to start and how everything fits together.

We updated the [main documentation](https://pymarkdown.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) and introduced new [Quick Start guides](https://pymarkdown.readthedocs.io/en/latest/quick-starts/) for common workflows. We simplified each section and reorganized the content so related topics are grouped together and easier to follow. Each Quick Start guide focuses on a single topic, helping new users get productive with PyMarkdown as quickly as possible. New users can now go from install to scanning a repository in just a few minutes. Existing users should find it easier to jump straight to the commands and options they need.

Going forward, you can expect faster scans, clearer error reporting, and continued improvements to the documentation. To support that, our primary goal is to deliver requested features and respond quickly to reported issues, particularly in the rule set, configuration, and documentation. Behind the scenes, we are reducing skipped tests, working through backlogged issues, and investing in refactoring and performance analysis. This work helps keep PyMarkdown fast and dependable as it grows.

##### Added

- [Issue 1511](https://redirect.github.com/jackdewinter/pymarkdown/issues/1511)
  - Added `plugins.per-file-ignores.*` configuration items to allow for rules to be disabled by matching against a glob-path.
- [Issue 1535](https://redirect.github.com/jackdewinter/pymarkdown/issues/1535)
  - Added documentation under the extensions section to provide information on the tables extension.

##### Changed

- [Issue 1527](https://redirect.github.com/jackdewinter/pymarkdown/issues/1527)
  - Updated documentation to give more examples, including examples of TOML configurations.
- [Issue 1539](https://redirect.github.com/jackdewinter/pymarkdown/issues/1539)
  - Did full sweep through existing documentation, to clean up.
- [Issue 1555](https://redirect.github.com/jackdewinter/pymarkdown/issues/1555)
  - Badges were out of sync, needed new mechanism to properly fetch

### [`v0.9.35`](https://redirect.github.com/jackdewinter/pymarkdown/releases/tag/v0.9.35): Version 0.9.35 - 2026-01-24

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jackdewinter/pymarkdown/compare/v0.9.34...v0.9.35)

This release was all about starting to clean up some long lingering items that had been on the to-do list for a while.  Before addressing  [Issue 1503](https://redirect.github.com/jackdewinter/pymarkdown/issues/1503), the file scanning code was moved out to the [application\_file\_scanner](https://redirect.github.com/\[jackdewinter/application_file_scanner]\(https://github.com/jackdewinter/application_file_scanner\)) project. This allowed our team to define a clean separation of responsibilities between the file scanning and the linting, something that we started with the [application\_properties](https://redirect.github.com/jackdewinter/application_properties) package. We had started that a while ago, so it was nice to be able to complete that task and to include the `--respect-ignore` functionality into that new package.

Our main goal for the next couple of months is to address new features and issues as they arise.  However, we hope to have enough time to reduce the number of skipped tests and backlogged issues in the repository, while also working on more refactoring and performance analysis.  I hope this helps you see the direction that we are taking this repository in!

#### Added

- [Issue 1503](https://redirect.github.com/jackdewinter/pymarkdown/issues/1503)
  - Added support for `--respect-gitignore` flags to respect any Git directories and their `.gitignore` files.

#### Fixed

- [Issue 1484](https://redirect.github.com/jackdewinter/pymarkdown/issues/1484)
  - Made [change](https://redirect.github.com/jackdewinter/application_properties/issues/318) in `application_properties` package to properly apply section header when using the `--config` flag.
  - Added tests to this repository to verify that both implicit and explicit TOML files can be used.

### [`v0.9.34`](https://redirect.github.com/jackdewinter/pymarkdown/releases/tag/v0.9.34): Version 0.9.34 - 2025-12-21

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jackdewinter/pymarkdown/compare/v0.9.33...v0.9.34)

##### Notes

Our team has been working diligently over the past two months to strengthen the foundation of the PyMarkdown Linter. A major milestone is the upgrade of the minimum Python version we test with from 3.9 to 3.10. While we acknowledge that some users may still prefer Python 3.8, we strongly recommend upgrading to 3.10 for improved compatibility, security, and performance. If you are using a version below 3.9 and have a valid reason to stay on that version, please let us know—we’ll explore options to support your needs.

A key feature addition (in response to [Issue 1479](https://redirect.github.com/jackdewinter/pymarkdown/issues/1479) ) is the full support for both the disable-next-line pragma and a new mode. This change ensures compatibility with Markdown formatters that add a blank line after HTML comments, as each rule now allows a single blank line between the pragma and the offending line. This update also required us to review and verify all rules to ensure the disable-next-line pragma suppresses issues on the next line effectively. During this process, we identified and fixed 9 critical issues related to pragmas and rule behavior.

Looking ahead, we’re also focused on long-term improvements to our test suite. Over the next six months, we aim to reduce the number of tests while maintaining full code and scenario coverage. As the project has been active for over five years, some tests have remained unchanged for three or more years. Our goal is to refine the test suite to ensure it remains efficient, maintainable, and aligned with our quality standards.

##### Added

- [Issue 1479](https://redirect.github.com/jackdewinter/pymarkdown/issues/1479)
  - Support for having a pragma to disable the rule for the next line is extended to include a single blank line between the pragma and
    the line where the failure occurs.
  - Added large number of tests (see work in fixed section) to ensure that next-line pragmas are consistently working for all rules.
- [Issue 1490](https://redirect.github.com/jackdewinter/pymarkdown/issues/1490)
  - Added work to measure "extra" test coverage, with goals to keep scenario coverage but reduce redundant code coverage
  - i.e. if two scenarios are different enough but have the same code coverage, have a way to mark them as such

##### Fixed

- [Issue 1426](https://redirect.github.com/jackdewinter/pymarkdown/issues/1426)

author: chriselsen
body:
This PR adds support for deploying CloudTAK as part of the TAK infrastructure deployment process.

## Changes

- Added a new configuration variable `DEPLOY_CLOUDTAK` (default: false) that can be set to true to enable CloudTAK deployment
- Added CloudTAK repository cloning when CloudTAK deployment is enabled
- Implemented CloudTAK deployment after TAK Server deployment
- Added CloudTAK destruction in the correct order when destroying infrastructure
- Added display of CloudTAK URL and admin credentials after deployment
- Added emptying of ELB logs bucket during stack destruction to prevent "bucket not empty" errors
- Updated README with information about CloudTAK deployment option

## How to Use

To enable CloudTAK deployment, set `DEPLOY_CLOUDTAK=true` at the top of the script. When enabled, the script will:

1. Clone the CloudTAK repository
2. Deploy CloudTAK after deploying TAK Server
3. Display the CloudTAK URL and admin credentials in the output

## Testing

Tested with both deployment and destruction workflows with CloudTAK enabled and disabled.

author: missingroberto
body:
Part of https://github.com/grafana/git-ui-sync-project/issues/347

## What

This PR automatically appends `.git` to repository URLs when creating a new RawClient in the protocol/client package.

## Why

Git servers typically require the `.git` extension for proper Git protocol endpoints. Without this extension, requests to endpoints like `/info/refs` or `/git-upload-pack` may fail or not be properly routed to the Git protocol handlers.

## How

- Modified `NewRawClient()` function to check if the URL path ends with `.git`
- If not, and the path is not empty (root path), append `.git` to the URL path
- Trims trailing slashes before appending to ensure clean URLs
- Added comprehensive unit tests covering various URL scenarios:
  - URLs with and without `.git` extension
  - URLs with trailing slashes
  - Root paths (which remain unchanged)
  - Complex paths with subgroups
- Updated existing tests to work with the new URL structure

## Remarks

- Root paths (e.g., `https://example.com`) remain unchanged to avoid creating invalid URLs
- The implementation is backward compatible - URLs that already end with `.git` are left unchanged
- All existing tests pass, ensuring no regression in functionality
- The change is transparent to users of the API

Examples:
- `https://github.com/owner/repo` → `https://github.com/owner/repo.git`
- `https://github.com/owner/repo.git` → `https://github.com/owner/repo.git` (unchanged)
- `https://example.com` → `https://example.com` (root path unchanged)

# Description
Implement Allu history event handling so that all events are stored in Haitaton - not just failed events as before.
Events are handled in correct order and marked as processed or failed.
Later events cannot be handled for an application until previous failed event is successfully processed.
Error in one event handling does not prevent from handling other events for other applications.
Old processed events are deleted (after 90 days as default).

author: sebastian-meckovski
body:
This pull request sets up a new Next.js project for a geo-lookup API, including configuration, environment setup, and API routes for city information retrieval. The changes include project initialization, API route implementations, utility functions, and configuration files.

### Project Setup and Configuration:

* **`.gitignore`**: Added rules to ignore common development, build, and environment files, including `node_modules`, `.env*`, and `.next/`.
* **`package.json`**: Defined project metadata, scripts for development (`dev`), build (`build`), and start (`start`), and added dependencies such as `mongodb`, `ngeohash`, and `next`.
* **`tsconfig.json`**: Configured TypeScript compiler options, including strict mode, module resolution, and path aliases.
* **`next.config.ts`**: Added a basic Next.js configuration file.
* **`vercel.json`**: Configured Vercel deployment settings for specific branches (`develop` and `master`).

### API Route Implementations:

* **`src/app/api/city-info-by-coordinates/route.ts`**: Implements an API endpoint to find the nearest city to given GPS coordinates using geohashing and the Haversine formula.
* **`src/app/api/city-info-by-ascii/route.ts`**: Implements an API endpoint to retrieve city information using country code and optional city/admin area names.
* **`src/app/api/search/route.ts`**: Implements an API endpoint for searching cities based on keywords using MongoDB Atlas Search.
* **`src/app/[slug]/route.ts`**: Adds a dynamic route to respond with a greeting message based on the URL slug. ([geo-lookup-next-js-api/src/app/[slug]/route.tsR1-R9](diffhunk://#diff-d2a4dca1236f64cfd5c470c1df5d7b31ee94637bd231997c2aaaa6868df0ebb9R1-R9))
* **`src/app/route.ts`**: Adds a root route that responds with a simple "Hello world!" message.

### Utility Functions:

* **`src/utils/haversine.ts`**: Implements the Haversine formula to calculate distances between two geographic points.
* **`src/utils/mongodb.ts`**: Sets up a reusable MongoDB client connection, handling development and production environments.

### Documentation:

* **`README.md`**: Provides project setup instructions, API endpoint details, and deployment guidance.

author: tjazerzen
body:
With Plain-Git integration for source and conformance test code set in place, we're introducing the ability to utilize and commit the generated code in the existing repositories.

## Destination folder for the generated code

### You can copy the source code to source code destination folder

Through the plain2code CLI, you can now set `--copy-build` (bool) argument, telling if you want to copy the source code into destination folder after a successful rendering. By default, this code is copied into `dist/` folder, but you can manage this through `--build-dest` CLI parameter.

### You can copy the conformance tests to source code destination folder

Through the plain2code CLI, you can now set `--copy-conformance-tests` (bool) argument, telling if you want to copy the conformance test code into conformance test destination folder after a successful rendering. By default, this code is copied into `dist_conformance_tests/`, but you can manage this through `--conformance-tests-dest` CLI parameter.

## Other Changes

- Raising threshold for max conformance test runs to `20`, ensuring smoother code generation
- Minor bugfixes

Introduces a new command that uses an LLM to determine if a next edit prediction should be triggered, based on recent edit history and current code context. Aims to reduce irrelevant or premature suggestions by considering the user's workflow and edit patterns before initiating prediction.

This pull request introduces a new gated prediction feature for the Next Edit extension, leveraging an AI model to decide whether to trigger predictions based on the user's recent editing context. Additionally, it includes minor refactoring to improve code readability and maintainability. 

### Gated Prediction Feature:

* [`src/api/predictionGate.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-86aa723ef94fa624fd5452e332a0649620fdc917979eafc338b4e61562761d0cR1-R89): Added a new `shouldTriggerNextEdit` function that uses OpenAI's GPT-4 model to determine whether a next edit prediction should be triggered based on the user's recent edit history and code excerpt. Includes logic for handling API errors and fallback behavior.
* [`src/commands/registerCommands.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-7aedfdde409c92096e09505c33a32ab6c61b36645e58da8a159ca63144f9c364R36-R58): Registered a new command `nextEdit.gatedPredict` that integrates the gated prediction logic into the extension. The command skips prediction if the AI model decides it is unnecessary, with appropriate logging and user feedback via the status bar.

### Command Registration Updates:

* [`package.json`](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519R25-R28): Added the new `nextEdit.gatedPredict` command to the list of available commands for the extension.

### Code Refactoring:

* [`src/controller/NextEditController.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-b44b41b90bdb7b735b3aea57794cc86eea7d726820468fe212afd38f8e62f2fcL32-R33): Replaced hardcoded context lines around cursor with a constant `CONTEXT_LINES_AFTER_CURSOR` for better configurability and readability.

- **Component Testing**: All 15 CompanyDetails tests passing

body:
I've tested this by starting up mod-agreements using the master-branch schema and dropping tenant. Then, I load in the packages and delete the "current" refDataValue for lifecycleStatus and "global" rdv for availabilityScope. I then run a diagnostic SQL query to check that some packages are indeed now pointing to the missing refDataValues. I then create the migration and run trigger-migrations, and check the packages table again and see that now all packages that were previously referencing "null" values in availabilityScope or lifecycleStatus are now pointing at the new "missingAvailabilityScope..."  values.

Finally, I go back to Bruno and try to delete a refDataValue for the lifecycleStatus or availabilityScope categories, and it fails because of the foreign key constraint. So think this is a success.

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements a complete overhaul of the MUPAI questionnaire system as requested, transforming it from a single old questionnaire to a modern, multi-questionnaire system with professional navigation and automated email integration.

## 🎯 Problem Statement
The existing system had an outdated energy balance questionnaire that needed to be replaced with a new advanced system while preserving the food preferences questionnaire and adding proper navigation and email functionality.

## ✨ Key Features Implemented

### 🏠 Professional Homepage with Navigation
![MUPAI Homepage](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f3881aa-2c31-4654-bbc7-510d2547cb08)

- Clean, branded interface with MUPAI styling
- Sidebar navigation for easy questionnaire selection
- Comprehensive information about each questionnaire
- Usage instructions and security warnings
- Professional contact information and version tracking

### ⚡ Advanced Energy Balance Questionnaire
![Balance Energético Form](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f4d24091-0856-49b8-ac89-f612843edca2)

- **Scientific calculations**: Automatic body composition adjustments by measurement method
- **Energy expenditure**: Complete GER, GEAF, GEE, and GET calculations
- **Sleep quality**: Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (abbreviated)
- **Stress assessment**: PSS-4 Perceived Stress Scale
- **Intelligent Recovery Factor (FRI)**: Automatic calculation based on sleep and stress
- **Automatic goal determination**: Based on body fat percentage, gender, and training level
- **Smart macronutrient allocation**: Personalized protein, fat, and carbohydrate distribution

### 🍽️ Food Preferences & Cravings Questionnaire
![Preferences Form](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66517200-71a9-4625-850c-7be0fbeb19b6)

- **Detailed food selection**: 6 organized food groups with specific options
- **Cravings analysis**: Sweet and savory preferences with triggers
- **Dietary restrictions**: Allergies, intolerances, and special diets
- **Personalization**: Custom dietary preferences and additional comments

## 🔧 Technical Improvements

### 📧 Automated Email System
- **Secure SMTP integration** with Zoho Mail
- **Automatic email sending** to `administracion@muscleupgym.fitness`
- **Comprehensive reports** with detailed analysis for each questionnaire
- **Production-ready configuration** using Streamlit secrets

### 🔒 Security & Production Readiness
- **Environment variables** for sensitive data
- **Secrets management** via Streamlit secrets
- **Configuration templates** for easy deployment
- **Comprehensive documentation** with setup instructions

### 🎨 User Experience
- **Intuitive sidebar navigation** for questionnaire selection
- **Professional styling** with consistent MUPAI branding
- **Real-time calculations** and feedback
- **Form validation** and error handling
- **Responsive design** for different screen sizes

## 📂 Files Changed

### Added Files
- `cuestionario_preferencias.py` - New food preferences questionnaire
- `README.md` - Comprehensive documentation
- `secrets_template.toml` - Production configuration template
- `.gitignore` - Security and build artifact exclusions

### Modified Files
- `app.py` - Complete rewrite with sidebar navigation system
- `newfile.py` - Enhanced advanced energy balance questionnaire with email integration

### Removed Files
- `cuestionario_fbeo.py` - Old energy balance questionnaire (as requested)

## 🚀 Production Deployment

The system includes complete production setup:

1. **SMTP Configuration**: Secure email credentials via secrets
2. **Environment Variables**: Production-ready configuration
3. **Documentation**: Complete setup and usage instructions
4. **Security**: No hardcoded credentials, proper secrets management

## 📊 System Architecture

```
MUPAI Sistema de Cuestionarios
├── Homepage (Inicio)
│   ├── System overview
│   ├── Questionnaire descriptions
│   └── Usage instructions
├── Advanced Energy Balance
│   ├── Scientific calculations
│   ├── Automatic email reporting
│   └── Intelligent recommendations
└── Food Preferences
    ├── Detailed food selection
    ├── Cravings analysis
    └── Dietary restrictions
```

## 🎯 Requirements Fulfilled

- ✅ **Completely removed** old energy balance questionnaire
- ✅ **Preserved** food preferences and cravings questionnaire
- ✅ **Added** new advanced automated energy balance questionnaire
- ✅ **Implemented** sidebar navigation for questionnaire selection
- ✅ **Added** individual submit buttons for each questionnaire
- ✅ **Integrated** automatic email sending via SMTP Zoho Mail
- ✅ **Secured** credentials using environment variables/secrets
- ✅ **Made** production-ready with configuration templates

## 📝 Next Steps

1. Configure SMTP credentials in production environment
2. Set up `.streamlit/secrets.toml` with real credentials
3. Deploy to production platform
4. Test email functionality with real SMTP server

The system is now ready for production use with a professional, secure, and user-friendly interface that meets all specified requirements.

*This pull request was created as a result of the following prompt from Copilot chat.*
> Implementar una nueva versión del sistema de cuestionarios en la app:
> 
> 1. Eliminar completamente el cuestionario antiguo de balance energético.
> 2. Conservar el cuestionario de preferencias y antojos alimentarios.
> 3. Agregar el nuevo cuestionario avanzado y automatizado de balance energético como sección principal.
> 4. Si existe un tercer cuestionario activo (especificar nombre), conservarlo.
> 5. Reorganizar la navegación de la app (por ejemplo, menú lateral en Streamlit) para que el usuario pueda elegir entre:
>    - "Cuestionario de Balance Energético" (nuevo, automatizado)
>    - "Preferencias y Antojos Alimentarios"
>    - (Tercer cuestionario si aplica)
> 6. Cada cuestionario debe tener su propio formulario y botón de "Enviar" (Submit).
> 7. Al hacer submit, las respuestas de cada cuestionario deben enviarse automáticamente al correo administracion@muscleupgym.fitness usando SMTP Zoho Mail.
> 8. El sistema debe ser seguro: NO exponer contraseñas directamente en el código (usar variables de entorno/streamlit secrets).
> 9. El código de ejemplo debe estar listo para producción y contener instrucciones de configuración segura de credenciales SMTP.
> 
> No eliminar ni modificar el cuestionario de preferencias y antojos alimentarios. Solo eliminar el viejo cuestionario de balance energético y agregar el nuevo como sección principal.

author: junkisai
body:
## Issue

- resolve: Refactor multi-agent message type system for better maintainability

## Why is this change needed?

The current timeline item type system has separate types for each agent (assistant_pm, assistant_db, assistant_qa). This change unifies the type system by using a single `assistant` type with a `role` field to distinguish between agents, improving code maintainability and extensibility.

### Changes Made

- Consolidated `assistant_pm`, `assistant_db`, `assistant_qa` types into a unified `assistant` type
- Added `role` field to identify agent roles ('pm' | 'db' | 'qa')
- Implemented role-based rendering using pattern matching in `TimelineItem` component
- Updated stories and tests to use the new type structure
- Improved error handling with conditional `onRetry` prop passing

### Technical Details

- Defined `AssistantRole` type ('pm' | 'db' | 'qa')
- Removed individual agent types from `TimelineItemEntry` union
- Updated `timelineUtils.ts` to generate unified agent entries
- Ensured type safety with pattern matching using `.exhaustive()`

This refactoring makes it easier to add new agent types and reduces code duplication while maintaining the same functionality.

author: copilot
body:
The `metric` property in `azurerm_monitor_diagnostic_setting` has been deprecated and will be removed in v5.0 of the AzureRM provider. This PR updates the diagnostic settings module to use the new `enabled_metric` property to ensure compatibility with AzureRM v5.0 and beyond.

## Changes Made

- **Updated `diagnostic-settings/diagnostic.tf`**: Replaced the deprecated `dynamic "metric"` block with `dynamic "enabled_metric"`
- **Updated iterator reference**: Changed `category = metric.value` to `category = enabled_metric.value`

## Before (deprecated syntax):
```hcl
dynamic "metric" {
  for_each = local.metrics == null ? [] : local.metrics
  content {
    category = metric.value
    enabled  = true
  }
}
```

## After (v5.0 compatible syntax):
```hcl
dynamic "enabled_metric" {
  for_each = local.metrics == null ? [] : local.metrics
  content {
    category = enabled_metric.value
    enabled  = true
  }
}
```

## Validation

- ✅ Terraform format check passed
- ✅ No other files required changes
- ✅ Minimal impact: only 2 lines changed in 1 file
- ✅ All existing functionality preserved
- ✅ Module interface remains unchanged (no breaking changes for users)

## Impact

This change ensures the diagnostic settings module will continue to work when upgrading to AzureRM provider v5.0, while maintaining full backward compatibility with existing configurations.

Fixes #40.

author: andrea-deri
body:
This PR contains a **proposal** for the `COSO (Catching Out-of-sync Operation)` application.  
The proposal aims to define a new API to reconcile individual BizEvents. Currently, this cannot be done because the process (manual or automatic) runs on a specific time-slot, operating on multiple elements in batch-mode. With this new API, it is possible to directly reconcile a single receipt and convert it into a BizEvent, with the precondition that no valid event has previously been generated by the automatic processes of the pagoPA platform.   
An interesting feature that this proposal also includes is the ability to search into the **historical** database, permitting the reconciliation of payments that, in any case, cannot be generated by current automatic processes or manual synchronisation. This functionality is defined _**only**_ for the synchronisation of single events, in order to avoid large, infinite queries not indexed on the historical DB.

#### List of Changes
 - Adding double persistence, permitting search in current DB instance and in historic DB instance
 - Including new API that permits to reconcile single receipts in BizEvents 

#### Motivation and Context
These changes are a proposal that helps to recover single error on unconverted receipts.

#### How Has This Been Tested?
 - Tested in local pointing to PROD databases

body:
This pull request refactors the `textlint-rule-allowed-uris` rule to improve modularity and maintainability by splitting the URI type handlers into separate functions. It also updates related tests to align with the new structure.

### Refactoring of URI type handling:

* In `src/textlint-rule-allowed-uris.js`, replaced the single `getUriTypes` function with modularized functions (`getUriTypesLink`, `getUriTypesImage`, `getUriTypesDefinition`, and `getUriTypesHtml`) for handling different node types. Updated the rule's entry point to utilize these modularized functions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7da72e1e0d5c49a43b94f9d928d3157918c0bdcc3121c5ed14e0bc459b3f26f9L2-R16) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7da72e1e0d5c49a43b94f9d928d3157918c0bdcc3121c5ed14e0bc459b3f26f9L20-R102)

* In `src/utils/get-uri-types/get-uri-types.js`, removed the monolithic `getUriTypes` function and exported the new modularized functions for retrieving URIs based on node types. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ae0ca24cd5da9be0ab68a39c227181c366ccf801a2e742976dbca35867112bccR29-R57) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ae0ca24cd5da9be0ab68a39c227181c366ccf801a2e742976dbca35867112bccL83-R90)

### Updates to tests:

* In `src/utils/get-uri-types/get-uri-types.test.js`, updated test cases to directly test the new modularized functions instead of the removed `getUriTypes` function. This ensures the tests are aligned with the refactored code. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4e8cad35eb168c20ef479b5e7b8262cc6c5449dd35828f86afbbdc407d73037bL12-R17) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4e8cad35eb168c20ef479b5e7b8262cc6c5449dd35828f86afbbdc407d73037bL64-R69) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4e8cad35eb168c20ef479b5e7b8262cc6c5449dd35828f86afbbdc407d73037bL326-R331) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-4e8cad35eb168c20ef479b5e7b8262cc6c5449dd35828f86afbbdc407d73037bL604-R609)

These changes improve code readability, make the codebase easier to maintain, and ensure that each function has a single responsibility.

author: copilot
body:
Fixes three critical user interface problems that were breaking the intended UX flow in the architectural elements management system.

## Issues Fixed

### Problem 1: Architectural Elements Value Loss ✅
**Issue**: When collapsing the "Список Архитектурные элементы" panel, the selected value was being reset visually but preserved in the generated text, creating confusion for users.

**Solution**: Enhanced the collapse/expand functionality to show the selected value in a condensed format when collapsed:
- Added collapsed state display element that preserves and shows the selected architectural element value
- Enhanced toggle functionality to update the display when selection changes
- Maintains actual dropdown selection state when expanding/collapsing

body:
## Description

I was trying to migrate a ROS 1 code to ROS 2 for a 2D application where it was necessary to create Quaternion msgs from yaw. This was possible back then with [createQuaternionMsgFromYaw](https://docs.ros.org/en/noetic/api/tf/html/c++/namespacetf.html#a09ddb5ff50f5032761feaa6a760f7344). I see a similar [utility function also in nav2_util](https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/blob/ee2d7789e70a968e6194af08030b425f3c591084/nav2_util/include/nav2_util/geometry_utils.hpp#L40).

To keep it a one liner in `tf2` I thought a constructor from RPY could help alot. This way, the abovementioned can be achieved with the following:

`geometry_msgs::msg::Quaternion quaternion_msg = tf2::toMsg(tf2::Quaternion(r,p,y))`

## Add Report Model, Schema, and Collection

### JIRA : https://jira.corp.adobe.com/browse/SITES-33568

### Summary

This PR introduces a new `Report` entity to the `spacecat-shared-data-access` package. The addition includes:

- The `Report` model class
- The `ReportCollection` collection class
- The ElectroDB schema definition for reports
- Integration with the entity registry
- Associated tests and fixtures

This enables CRUD operations and queries for report data, supporting features such as fetching by site, report type, and ID.

---

### Highlights

- **Model:** `Report` (extends `BaseModel`)
- **Collection:** `ReportCollection` (extends `BaseCollection`)
- **Schema:** Defines required attributes and validation for reports
- **Indexes:** Supports querying by `siteId` (`belongs_to` Site)
- **Tests:** Integration and unit tests for report creation, retrieval, and validation
- **Fixtures:** Example report data for testing

### Recent Updates

#### Schema Enhancement: Optional storagePath with Auto-computation
- **Made `storagePath` optional**: Changed from `required: true` to `required: false` with `default: () => ''`
- **Smart auto-computation**: Empty storage paths are automatically computed using pattern `/reports/{siteId}/{reportType}/{reportId}/`
- **Enhanced validation**: Accepts empty strings, undefined, null, and non-empty strings; rejects non-string types
- **Backward compatibility**: Existing reports with storage paths continue to work
- **Custom path support**: Custom storage paths are preserved and not overridden
- **Updateable**: Storage paths remain updateable after creation

#### Test Coverage
- **Integration tests**: Added tests for custom storage paths and auto-computed scenarios
- **Unit tests**: Enhanced collection tests to verify optional behavior
- **Schema validation tests**: Comprehensive tests for all validation scenarios
- **All tests passing**: 27/27 tests (13 unit + 7 integration + 7 schema validation)

author: assassintee
body: Without putting quad layers into a group with clipping enabled, we need to check every quad if it needs to be rendered. This can be very exhaustive with huge quad layers, which is the reason why the quad-pixelart-tool adds a group and calculates clipping. This PR introduces automatic (optional) clipping to a quad layer itself, which gets calculated on map-setup-time. This might improve FPS, because it just skips rendering the layer if a player is outside the clipping region. This works best in maps, where a huge amount of quads are regional. It is also a step towards quad clustering. The clip region calculation also takes envelopes into account. **Caveats:** - Clipping is only done to grouped quad layers (all quads containing the same Envs), because otherwise the calculation gets too expensive. You'd need to calculate every minimum and maximum position offset for every Env in advance. - Rotation disables the automatic clipping, because you can't easily determine offsets with envelope points anymore. (The quad itself can be rotated, this is only about rotation in envelopes) - Bezier curves are not clipped perfectly, but reasonably approximated **Screenshots:** - Envelopeless quads clipping region - pixel art test **Videos:** - perfect clipping for linear envelopes https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b048a309-c3c2-4d20-ab06-9cc69033f3bd - imperfect clipping for bezier envelopes https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/535daa65-4934-4ae6-b708-92d2294144da **Test maps:** - linear test in attachment - bezier test in attachment - unclipped mona lisa in attachment, **do not open in editor if you don't have a powerful computer** - `Abyss` and `CyberSpace` might be good ddnet test maps [quad-clip-test-maps.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21291723/quad-clip-test-maps.zip) **Debugging clip region:** The red line shown in the image is **not** part of the PR and are only there to show, that this feature is tested and working. If you wish to debug quad clipping, add this lines to the end of `CQuadRenderLayer::Render`: ```C++ if(m_QuadRenderGroup.m_Clipped) { Graphics()->TextureClear(); Graphics()->LinesBegin(); Graphics()->SetColor(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f); IGraphics::CLineItem LineItems[4] = { IGraphics::CLineItem(m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipX, m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipY, m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipX, m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipY + m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipHeight), IGraphics::CLineItem(m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipX + m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipWidth, m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipY, m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipX + m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipWidth, m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipY + m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipHeight), IGraphics::CLineItem(m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipX, m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipY, m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipX + m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipWidth, m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipY), IGraphics::CLineItem(m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipX, m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipY + m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipHeight, m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipX + m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipWidth, m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipY + m_QuadRenderGroup.m_ClipHeight), }; Graphics()->LinesDraw(LineItems, 4); Graphics()->LinesEnd(); } ``` **Benchmarks:** I did see improvements in the released ddnet maps, but only minor ones. I could do a proper analysis of multiple maps to show some benefits if requested. You can clearly see a difference on the mona lisa map, which is admittedly more of an outlier map. **Last words:** The rendering now cries for proper quad grouping ## Checklist - [x] Tested the change ingame - [x] Provided screenshots if it is a visual change - [ ] Tested in combination with possibly related configuration options - [ ] Written a unit test (especially base/) or added coverage to integration test - [ ] Considered possible null pointers and out of bounds array indexing - [ ] Changed no physics that affect existing maps - [ ] Tested the change with [ASan+UBSan or valgrind's memcheck](https://github.com/ddnet/ddnet/#using-addresssanitizer--undefinedbehavioursanitizer-or-valgrinds-memcheck) (optional)

Fix improper handling of laser power values across GRBL and Ruida backends and ensure correct power propagation during plotting, while also enhancing emulator stop commands and cleaning up related code.

- Initialize PlotCut instances with the correct power settings and use absolute power for plot_append in both GRBL and Ruida jobs
- Clamp and store power values in the `lihuiyu` driver and prevent inadvertent power resets in PlotCut initialization
- Standardize the prefix formatting in Ruida process output

Enhancements:
- Enable grblserver and ruidaserver to handle 'stop'/'quit' commands via a remainder argument
- Refine plugin extended_info strings, remove leftover debug prints, and apply minor code style improvements

body:
Fixes #228.

This should allow users to provide their own types implementing `flag.Value` also to `pflag`, as `pflag.Value` is now equivalent to the standard-library variant.

The `Type()` method is moved to a wrapper interface `TypedValue` and code relying on it must first test that the provided value implements this interface; this has been done in all code in `pflag` and tests are still passing, so I'm fairly confident that the changes are correct even if I haven't actually tried them out on a use case with a user-defined `Value` implementation (without `Type()`).
